You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The structure is described in a nonstandard input cell with lattice parameters a = 5.02608422 Å, b = 6.082960000000001 Å, c = 6.68326618 Å, α = 117.06936493000002°, β = 102.97141533999998°, and γ = 89.99847659999999°, containing 14 atoms with the declared composition Na₂V₄O₈. The underlying symmetry is space group number 15, C2/c (Hall symbol −C 2yc), and the conventional standard fractional coordinates q_standard are obtained from the input fractional coordinates q_input through q_standard = P q_input + s, where the first row of P is (3.168965197060732×10⁻¹⁸, −1.5237248141085692×10⁻¹⁸, −0.49999999999999994), the second row is (−3.168965197060732×10⁻¹⁸, −1.0, 0.49999999999999994), the third row is (−1.0, −5.6939469619484865×10⁻¹⁸, −1.1550426341664848×10⁻¹⁸), and the origin shift s is (1.4999999999876223×10⁻⁶, −1.4999999999876223×10⁻⁶, 0.0). Input positional values were rounded to six decimal places before the listed corrections.

In the standard C2/c description, sodium occupies the single fourfold 4e orbit with coordinate relation (0, y, 1/4); its representative site is (0.0, 0.301013, 0.25), so the only independent positional parameter is y = 0.301013. Vanadium occupies one general 8f orbit with representative position (0.24667700000000004, 0.3674210000000002, 0.762067), giving independent parameters x = 0.24667700000000004, y = 0.3674210000000002, and z = 0.762067. Oxygen is split between two crystallographically independent general 8f orbits. The first oxygen orbit has representative (0.1536169999999999, 0.3803660000000002, 0.026658999999999988), with independent parameters x = 0.1536169999999999, y = 0.3803660000000002, and z = 0.026658999999999988. The second oxygen orbit has representative (0.16450049999999994, 0.1201175000000001, 0.525439), with independent parameters x = 0.16450049999999994, y = 0.1201175000000001, and z = 0.525439. These four orbits account for the full standard-cell content through their multiplicities: four Na, eight V, and sixteen O atoms in the conventional C-centered cell, while the supplied primitive-like input cell contains two Na, four V, and eight O atoms.

A V atom at (0.262067, 0.879256, 0.493357) is displaced by (3.500000000000725×10⁻⁵, −1.0000000000065512×10⁻⁵, −2.0999999999993246×10⁻⁵). A second V atom at (0.762067, 0.614098, 0.493357) is displaced by (−3.000000000086267×10⁻⁶, 9.999999999177334×10⁻⁷, −4.999999999977245×10⁻⁶). A third V atom at (0.737933, 0.120744, 0.506649) is displaced by (−3.2999999999949736×10⁻⁵, 9.999999999996123×10⁻⁶, 1.399999999995849×10⁻⁵).

The oxygen corrections are as follows. An O atom at (0.526659, 0.773251, 0.307237) is displaced by (−3.100000000000325×10⁻⁵, 8.000000000008×10⁻⁶, −6.999999999979245×10⁻⁶). An O atom at (0.973341, 0.466017, 0.692769) is displaced by (6.999999999979245×10⁻⁶, 0.0, −5.999999999950489×10⁻⁶). An O atom at (0.473341, 0.226749, 0.692769) is displaced by (2.4999999999997247×10⁻⁵, −7.000000000007001×10⁻⁶, 1.0000000000287557×10⁻⁶). An O atom at (0.025439, 0.044383, 0.329004) is displaced by (−1.8000000000000654×10⁻⁵, −7.000000000000062×10⁻⁶, −6.0000000000060005×10⁻⁶). An O atom at (0.525439, 0.284618, 0.329004) is displaced by (−5.999999999950489×10⁻⁶, −9.999999999732445×10⁻⁷, −6.0000000000060005×10⁻⁶). Finally, an O atom at (0.974561, 0.955617, 0.671002) is displaced by (2.4000000000024002×10⁻⁵, 6.999999999979245×10⁻⁶, 0.0). Together with the stated frame transformation, these values recover the original input-cell geometry rather than replacing it by an exactly idealized space-group model.
